description: Multi-dimensional adversarial review of a diff or capability: correctness, security, and spec compliance, with every finding adversarially verified before it is reported.

findings.title: Task screen returns a raw 500 when an admin removes hints from a published task after the child opened some
findings.evidence: `TaskView.hints.opened` is built as `(1..screen.hintsOpened).map { hint(task, it, locale) }`, and `hint()` reads `task.hints[index - 1]`. `hintsOpened` comes from the append-only `opened_hint` log, but `task.hints` is the current content. `TaskService.update` / `MissionRules.taskEdit` (Missions.kt:228) let an admin edit the content of a published task, including its hints. Say the child opened 2 hints and the task now has 1: `hints[1]` throws IndexOutOfBoundsException. getTask, getCurrentTask and startReplay then return a raw 500, and `remaining = task.hints.size - index` would go negative.
findings.suggestion: Clamp the opened count to the current number of hints: `(1..minOf(screen.hintsOpened, task.hints.size))`. Clamp `remaining` at 0 too. Add an IT that opens hints, removes them in an admin edit, and reloads the task.

findings.title: An old replay run comes back to life when a task is added to the mission later, so attempts go into the replay scope instead of the primary one
findings.evidence: `currentRun` takes the latest `practice_run` and treats it as active if `mission.taskIds.any { states[it]?.resolved != true }`, using the mission's current task list. Suppose a replay finished and the admin then adds a task (missions can be edited). The finished run now has an unresolved task, so it counts as the current replay again. getCurrentTask and submit then write that task's attempts into the replay scope with `replay=true`. The primary scope never sees the task, so HQ shows the mission IN_PROGRESS with a continue target that can't be cleared through the normal flow.
findings.suggestion: Mark a run as finished once it is complete: store `completed_at`, or freeze the run's task list when it starts. Or only treat a run as current when the tasks it started with are still unresolved. Then route newly added tasks to the primary scope.

findings.title: Summary first-try count leaves out shared tasks that were solved first try in a different mission
findings.evidence: `firstTry = attempts.count { it.attemptNo == 1 && it.correct && it.missionId == mission.missionId }`. In the primary scope one task's state is shared by every mission that contains it (OQ-15), so it can be resolved under another mission. That task counts in `taskCount = mission.taskIds.size` and makes the mission COMPLETE, but the `missionId` filter drops it from `firstTryCount`. The summary then shows something like '3 of 5 first try' even though all 5 were solved first try.
findings.suggestion: Count from the task states in the scope instead of filtering attempts by missionId: `states(scope, mission.taskIds).count { it.value == TaskState.CORRECT_FIRST_TRY }`. If the filter is intended, state that in the spec and design doc.

findings.title: Image read failure is not handled, so the child image endpoint can return a raw 500
findings.evidence: `storage.open(image.storageKey)?.use { it.readAllBytes() }` handles a missing file (null → 404). It does not handle an IOException from the storage adapter while reading (truncated or unreadable file, permissions). That exception reaches `getChildImage` without a handler in PracticeProblemAdvice and becomes a generic 500. The whole image is also read into memory inside a read-only DB transaction.
findings.suggestion: Catch IOException in `image()`: log it without the key contents and return null (404), or map it to a 5xx RFC 7807 problem with a human message. You could also stream the resource outside the transaction.

findings.title: HQ topics are listed in mission-list order instead of a defined order
findings.evidence: `missions.groupBy { it.topicId }.map { ... }` keeps topics in the order their first mission appears in `missions.list()`. Missions inside a topic are sorted by position, but topics are never sorted. Topic order on HQ therefore depends on how the store happens to return missions, and can change after edits.
findings.suggestion: Sort topics explicitly (topic position or name, whichever the practice-flow spec defines) before mapping them to `TopicView`.

findings.title: ServedContent.missions() runs one topic lookup and per-task lookups for every mission on each HQ load
findings.evidence: `served(mission, …)` calls `topics.find(mission.content.topicId)` once per mission. `mission(missionId)` passes `::servable`, which calls `tasks.find(taskId)` for each task. Every child endpoint goes through `mission()`, so each request does N task loads, including images, before running further `store.attempts` queries. `outcome()` re-reads every task's attempts again through `states()`.
findings.suggestion: Batch these: load the topics once per `missions()` call, and check servable tasks with a single filtered query, as `servableIds()` already does. That's fine for MVP data sizes, but worth doing before slice 8 adds XP aggregation.

findings.title: Unauthenticated, unthrottled child write endpoints let any LAN device burn attempts, force reveals and flood problem reports permanently
findings.evidence: The shared chain is `authorize(anyRequest, permitAll)` with CSRF off (SecurityConfiguration.kt:64-66), and the five child writes (attempt, hint, report, replay, ackRankUp) have no rate limit or per-device bound. Any device on the home network can read mission/task UUIDs from `GET /api/child/hq`, then submit two wrong attempts per task to turn every task REVEALED, open every hint, and start replay runs. Because the attempt log, opened hints and runs are append-only (FR-42, `V4__practice.sql`), the admin cannot undo this. The child's progress and stats are corrupted for good. `report()` inserts one `problem_report` row (note up to 1000 code points) per call with no cap, so a loop can grow the table and the admin report queue without limit. Every call also takes the global `pg_advisory_xact_lock` (JdbcPracticeStore.kt:18-24), so a flood blocks the real child too. Login-free child endpoints are by design (NFR-1), so this is limited to the LAN, but the scope asked about abuse resistance.
findings.suggestion: Add a simple in-process rate limit on `/api/child/**` POSTs (for example a token bucket keyed by remote address) and a cap on open problem reports per task (for example refuse with 409 once N OPEN reports exist for a task in a short window). Record the decision in design.md. Optionally give the admin a way to see where attempts came from, without logging any payload.

findings.title: 400 problem responses echo attacker-chosen JSON keys back in `errors[].field`
findings.evidence: `Grading.shapeErrors` returns `FieldError("answers.$key", "unknown-part")` for any submitted key that is not a part key, and `PracticeReaders.answers` builds `val field = "answers.$key"` (PracticeReaders.kt:28) for shape and length errors. `PracticeProblemAdvice.invalid` copies `it.field` into the response verbatim. A client can therefore put any string of up to about 16 KB, such as markup or a long text, into the problem JSON. That contradicts the file's own rule "never quote a submitted value (NFR-3)". The response is application/problem+json, so there is no direct XSS. The risk is a frontend that renders `field` as HTML, or a future log of problem bodies that captures child-typed content.
findings.suggestion: Report only part keys the task actually defines. For unknown keys, emit one generic error with field `answers` and code `unknown-part`, or truncate and sanitise the key to the contract's part-key pattern before echoing it. Add a test that a submitted key with markup or over 64 chars does not appear in the response.

findings.title: Checklist areas reviewed and found clean (informational, no action)
findings.evidence: Non-findings, listed so nothing is assumed by silence. (1) AuthZ/IDOR: every child route goes through `PracticeService.mission()` and `task()`. These require a PUBLISHED mission and a task in that mission's served list. `image()` resolves the owner task and requires PUBLISHED, TEXT and membership in a published mission (ServedContentService.kt:42-48). Child endpoints write only practice tables, never content. Answer keys: `ServedPart.spec` is never mapped into `TaskView`/`PartView`. `revealedAnswers` comes only from DeterministicTutor when the state is REVEALED. Format tips are built so they never fall in the accepted region (FormatTips.kt). The PracticeBodyAdvice placeholder binding prevents mass assignment. Single-tenant app, so there is no tenant scoping to check. (2) Auth/session: no change to admin auth; the ContentBodyAdvice narrowing still covers every content controller. (3) Injection: all new SQL in JdbcPracticeStore and JdbcTaskStore.imageOwner uses bound parameters; JSONB uses `?::jsonb` with a serialized tree. Images are served with an allowlisted PNG/JPEG media type and the default Spring Security nosniff header. The 16 KB body cap is enforced before parsing. No CSV/HTML rendering on the server. (4) Exposure: compose and CORS are not changed in this diff, and the Host firewall still blocks DNS rebinding. (5) Privacy: the display name is read through a function (not a dumped property). Spring JDBC and Hibernate ORM bind loggers are now capped at INFO. No PII or workbook content in the new migration or messages. (6) Secrets: none added. (7) Dependencies: pom.xml and package files are unchanged in d1843b0..HEAD, so there are no new advisories to assess for this slice. A full `mvn dependency-check` was not run.
findings.suggestion: None. Keep these properties covered by the existing PracticeIT and PracticeLogCaptureIT tests.

findings.title: Coverage summary: 47 backend scenarios: 41 implemented, 4 partial, 0 missing, 2 contradicted (both minor ordering/validation edges). XP, rank and mission-summary scenarios are deferred to slice 8 as placeholders, as the proposal declares.
findings.evidence: All 7 change-delta scenarios are implemented and tested (PracticeIT, PracticeRulesTest, TutorTest, TutorSwapTest). Of the 40 or so backend-relevant scenarios in contract/openspec/specs/practice-flow/spec.md, 4 are only partly covered: NFR-5 RTT, TC-6 network-denied, replay of an in-progress mission, and same-feedback across two fresh runs. 2 edge cases contradict the spec: 400 is returned before the 404 check, and the note limit is checked after trimming. Every FR the plan assigns to backend for practice-flow (FR-22, 24–31, 42, 44, plus FR-56, NFR-1 and NFR-5) has an @trace'd test.
findings.suggestion: No action on its own; see the individual findings.

findings.title: NFR-5 check round-trip test does not follow the scenario's fixture or load shape
findings.evidence: The scenario says: "Docker Compose stack seeded with a fixture of at least 10 published tasks that together cover every MVP answer type and include at least one two-part task … each a valid attempt 1 or attempt 2 … (fresh runs come from replays)". The test seeds a single INTEGER+DECIMAL task, runs `jdbc.update("DELETE FROM attempt")` after every request (line 116), so every submission is attempt 1, and runs against the in-process Spring Boot test server, not the Compose stack. CHOICE/TEXT/FRACTION paths and the attempt-2 lock path are never timed. The reported p95 of 67 ms is real but measures a narrower workload than the spec.
findings.suggestion: Seed 10 or more tasks covering every answer type. Alternate attempt 1 and attempt 2 using replays (startReplay) instead of deleting rows. Either run the measurement against the Compose stack (or the e2e job), or amend NFR-5's scenario to accept the in-process measurement as the backend half.

findings.title: TC-6 'Feedback never comes from AI' is only half enforced: no network-denied run of the attempt tests
findings.evidence: The scenario says: "…and the attempt-checking integration tests run with all outbound network connections from the backend container denied … every attempt-checking test passes with the network denied (TC-6)". TutorTest only has `no AI or LLM library is a dependency (TC-6)`, which inspects dependencies. Nothing in src/test or the battery denies outbound network during PracticeIT.
findings.suggestion: Add a mechanism that denies egress while the attempt ITs run, for example a Testcontainers network with internal=true for an app container, or a SecurityManager/ProxySelector guard that fails on any non-localhost socket. Otherwise record an explicit waiver in the store spec.

findings.title: Malformed body on a task that is not served returns 400, not the required 404
findings.evidence: The spec requires: "Every child request that names a task — … submitting an attempt, … reporting a problem — SHALL be refused with HTTP 404 … when the task does not exist, is not served…". In the code, `PracticeReaders.answers(body())` and `PracticeReaders.report(body())` run in the controller before `service.submit/report` looks up the mission or task (the PracticeReaders KDoc says "Checks that need no task run here, before any lookup"). So a 21-element list or an OTHER report without a note sent for a draft or GRAPHIC task gets 400, which shows the endpoint shape exists for unserved ids. Nothing is stored either way.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the mission and task (404) before validating the body, or amend the spec to say body-shape 400 takes precedence over 404. Add an IT that sends an invalid body for a draft task.

findings.title: Report note limit is checked after trimming, so notes over 1000 code points with surrounding whitespace are accepted
findings.evidence: The spec says: "The API SHALL refuse with HTTP 400 … a report note longer than 1000 code points (the `ReportRequest.note` limit in `api/openapi.yaml`)". The code does `is JsonText.Value -> note.text.trim().ifEmpty { null }`, then `if (text != null && text.codePointCount(...) > NOTE_MAX)`. A 1001-code-point note padded with whitespace, or 1000 characters plus a trailing space, passes, which is looser than the OpenAPI maxLength. The change delta says "the trimmed note" for storage, but not for validation.
findings.suggestion: Check the length on the raw note (matching the OpenAPI maxLength) and store the trimmed note. Alternatively, amend the spec/OpenAPI to say the limit applies after trimming. Add a test with a 1001-character note that has trailing whitespace.

findings.title: Locked parts are stored with raw = null on attempt 2, while the delta requires raw input verbatim per part
findings.evidence: The change delta says: "Each graded attempt SHALL be stored … with the raw input verbatim and the normalized input per part". The code has `records += PartRecord(part.key, null, lockedPart.normalized, Verdict.CORRECT, locked = true)`, so whatever the child sent for a locked part (e.g. `13` in the 'Locked part resent' scenario) is dropped from the attempt log. The store spec says the value is "ignored and not re-graded" but says nothing about not logging it, so this is undocumented drift in the attempt-log contents (progress-stats).
findings.suggestion: Either store the sent raw value (or explicitly mark it absent) for locked parts, or amend the delta/progress-stats 'Attempt log contents' to say locked parts carry no raw input on attempt 2.

findings.title: 'Replay of an unfinished mission is refused' is only tested for a NEW mission, not one in progress
findings.evidence: The scenario reads: "GIVEN a mission in progress / WHEN a replay request … THEN 409 … and the mission's progress is unchanged". The test calls `mvc.post("/api/child/missions/$m/replay").isProblem(409)` before any activity, so the mission is NEW. The code (PracticeService.kt:221 `if (primaryProgress(mission).state != MissionState.COMPLETE) throw PracticeConflict`) does handle IN_PROGRESS, but that path has no test and nothing asserts the progress is unchanged.
findings.suggestion: Add an IT that resolves one task, then requests a replay and asserts 409, that no practice_run row was created, and that resolvedCount is unchanged.

findings.title: 'Same input, same feedback' is verified only at unit level, not across two fresh runs through the API
findings.evidence: The scenario reads: "two fresh runs of the same task with the same hints opened … the `feedback` objects … byte-identical after JSON canonicalization, and the `parts` lists are equal in every key, verdict, normalized, formatTip and locked value". TutorTest `same input, same feedback` calls DeterministicTutor directly. No IT compares two serialized AttemptResults, for example a primary run against a replay run, so mapping or serialization nondeterminism such as RevealedAnswers ordering would not be caught.
findings.suggestion: Add an IT: submit the same wrong attempt 1 in two runs (two missions sharing the task, or primary plus replay) with equal hints opened, then compare the canonicalized `feedback` JSON and the `parts` arrays.

findings.title: Undocumented 400 for non-UUID path ids on endpoints whose OpenAPI lists only 200/404 (or 200/204/404)
findings.evidence: `@ExceptionHandler(MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException::class) fun typeMismatch(...) = invalid(request, listOf(FieldError(exception.name, "not-uuid")))` returns 400 for every child controller. contract/api/openapi.yaml declares no 400 for getMissionBriefing, getCurrentTask, startReplay, getMissionSummary, getTask, openNextHint or getChildImage (only 200/204/404/409). The instructions say the implementation must not use undocumented status codes.
findings.suggestion: Either map a malformed id to 404 NotFound, which matches "a mission id that does not exist", or add `400: BadRequest` to those operations in the docs-store OpenAPI and bump the contract pin.

findings.title: No backend test for the 413 'Request body too large' scenario on rank-up acknowledgement
findings.evidence: The scenario reads: "GIVEN any child endpoint that accepts a body (attempt, report, profile settings, rank-up acknowledgement) … THEN 413". PracticeIT tests 413 for attempts (line 565) and reports (line 721). ackRankUp is covered by PracticeBodyAdvice's PLACEHOLDERS map in code, but there is no test sending more than 16 KB to `/api/child/hq/rank-up-ack`.
findings.suggestion: Add a 17 KB rank-up-ack request to the replay/placeholder test asserting 413 problem+json.

result.reasoning:
Confirmed; the only error is the line number. The code is at PracticeMapping.kt:118 (the file is about 165 lines, so line 702 can't exist), with the hint helper at lines 155-163.

How it fails:
1. PracticeService.screen (PracticeService.kt:282) sets hintsOpened = store.hints(run.scope, [taskId]).size. That count comes from the append-only opened-hint log for the current run.
2. The task comes from served.task(taskId) (PracticeService.kt:255), which returns the task's current content, not a snapshot.
3. PracticeMapping.kt:118 builds the opened list as (1..screen.hintsOpened).map { hint(task, it, locale) }. Line 161 then reads task.hints[index - 1] without checking bounds (the translation lookup uses getOrNull, but the main list does not). Line 162 computes remaining = task.hints.size - index, which goes negative.
4. Nothing stops an admin from removing hints. TaskService.update (TaskService.kt:132-142) only runs MissionRules.taskEdit, which (Missions.kt:228-241) only refuses a change of topic or grade while the task is in a mission, or a switch to GRAPHIC while it is in a published mission. It has no "used" check and no rule about hints. The "used" check (usage.usedTasks) applies only to deletes.
5. No handler catches IndexOutOfBoundsException. The @ExceptionHandler methods in PracticeProblemAdvice and the other advice classes cover only specific exception types, so the error becomes an unhandled 500. That breaks the AGENTS.md rule that no input may produce a raw 500.

Who is affected: every caller of screen(), which includes getTask, getCurrentTask and replay. Example: a child opens 2 hints, the admin saves the task with 1 hint, and every later load of that task returns a 500 until a new run starts. Opening another hint does not crash: openHint returns a 409 because opened >= task.hints.size. The task screen itself stays broken.

Severity stays major: an ordinary admin edit leaves a child's task permanently unloadable. The suggested fix is correct: limit the opened count to the current number of hints and keep remaining at 0 or more.

The mechanism is real. One correction: the code is at PracticeMapping.kt:118 and :155-163, not line 702.

- **The crash:** line 118 builds `opened = (1..screen.hintsOpened).map { hint(task, it, locale) }`. `hint()` at line 161 reads `task.hints[index - 1]` without a bounds check, and line 162 computes `remaining = task.hints.size - index`.
- **Where `hintsOpened` comes from:** PracticeService.kt:282 sets it to `store.hints(run.scope, listOf(task.taskId)).size`. That is a count of the append-only opened-hint log, not of the current hints.
- **Where `task.hints` comes from:** ServedContentService.kt:96 maps it from the task's current content (`hints = c.hints`). There is no per-attempt snapshot.
- **No guard on edits:** `TaskService.update` (TaskService.kt:132-141) only checks `MissionRules.taskEdit` (Missions.kt:228-241). That refuses only topic/grade changes while the task is in missions, and switching to GRAPHIC while it is in a published mission. Nothing stops an admin from shortening the hints list of a published task the child has already used. The only usage-based guard (`usage.usedTasks`) applies to delete, not update.
- **Only the opening path is guarded:** PracticeService.kt:184 checks `opened >= task.hints.size` when opening a new hint. The rendering path has no check.

Repro: the child opens 2 hints, then the admin saves the task with 1 hint. The task stays published and servable, so GET of the task screen hits `hints[1]` and throws IndexOutOfBoundsException. That is an unhandled exception, so the child gets a 500, which breaks the "no raw 500" rule. Through getCurrentTask it can also block the child's mission until the admin adds the hints back.

It can't be triggered by an attacker; it needs an ordinary admin edit. But a single admin editing a hint wording or count is a normal authoring action, so a real user can easily reproduce it. Severity stays major, because it blocks the child's practice flow.

I couldn't refute the core mechanism. One part of the finding goes too far.

**Where the run is chosen.** `PracticeService.currentRun` is at `PracticeService.kt:258-262`, not line 1645. It takes `store.runs(missionId).lastOrNull()` and checks it against the mission's *current* `mission.taskIds`. If any of those tasks is unresolved in that run's scope, it returns `Run(run.id, replay=true)`. Runs have no completion marker and no frozen task list.

**Missions can gain tasks after publishing.** `MissionRules.edit` (`content/domain/Missions.kt:205-215`) lets a published mission take newly added tasks, as long as they are published text tasks. `ServedContentService.served` (`ServedContentService.kt:70-79`) builds `ServedMission.taskIds` straight from the stored mission's current list. So the next `served.mission()` call includes the added task.

**What happens after the edit.** Take a replay that finished, then an admin adds task T:
- `currentRun` now finds T unresolved in the old run and returns that run as replay.
- `currentTask`, `task`, `submit`, `openHint`, `report` and `briefing` all route through `currentRun`.
- `submit` therefore saves T's attempts with `scope=run.id` and `replay=true` (lines 136-167).
- `primaryProgress` only reads `Scope.PRIMARY`, so HQ shows IN_PROGRESS with T as the continue target.
- `briefing` mixes the two: task states come from the replay scope, but `state` comes from the primary scope.
- `replay()` returns the revived run unchanged, because `current.replay` is true.

**What the finding overstates.** It says the continue target "can't be cleared through the normal flow". That's wrong. Once the child resolves T in the revived run, every task in that run is resolved. `currentRun` then falls back to PRIMARY, and `currentTask` serves T again in the primary scope. So it does clear, but the child has to do the task twice, and the first attempts are logged as replay attempts. The misrouting is real; the permanent stuck state is not.

**Scope and severity.** The bug needs a published mission edited after a replay finished, which is a plausible admin action. The finding also misses that it happens whenever a replay run exists, even if the primary run had not finished when the task was added. The consequences are wrong attempt scope/flag and HQ inconsistent with what the child is shown, and they correct themselves after the double work. I'm keeping the severity at major for the data-integrity problem (attempts saved with the wrong scope and replay flag), with the caveat about recovery.

I confirmed the mechanism in the code. It can be reached through normal admin actions.

1. `PracticeService.kt:258-262`: `currentRun` takes the latest `practice_run` row. It decides whether that run is active by checking the mission's current `taskIds` against the run's states. A run has no `completed_at` field and no frozen task list, so a finished run is never marked as finished.
2. Admins can add tasks to a published mission. `content/domain/Missions.kt:202-203` says a published mission "stays non-empty and admits only published text tasks. Reordering and removing (while one remains) are always allowed". Adding a published TEXT task is therefore allowed. `ServedContentService` then serves the longer task list to the child right away.
3. Here is how to reproduce it. The child completes mission M, starts a replay with `replay()` and finishes it, so the run is complete. The admin then adds a published task T to M. Now `currentRun(M)` sees that T is unresolved in the old run and returns `Run(oldRun, replay=true)`. In `hq()`, which only reads the primary scope, M shows as IN_PROGRESS with `continueTarget` = T. When the child opens T, `task()`, `currentTask()`, `submit()` and `openHint()` all call `currentRun`. They show T in the replay scope and write the attempts and hints to `oldRun` with `replay=true`. `briefing()` mixes the two scopes: the state comes from the primary scope and the per-task states come from the replay scope. `replay()` also returns this revived run instead of starting a fresh one.

One overstatement: the finding says the continue target "can't be cleared through the normal flow." That is not quite true. Once T is resolved in the revived replay run, every task in the run is resolved again. `currentRun` then falls back to the primary scope. HQ still points at T, and the child can solve it again in the primary scope. So the state isn't stuck forever. What does happen is that the work goes into the wrong scope, the child has to solve the task twice, the replay flag and the summary are wrong, and the briefing shows inconsistent state. The data in the attempt log is also wrong (FR-31 logging is attributed to the wrong scope). The core problem is real and can be reproduced with normal admin and child actions, so I'm keeping the severity at major.

The finding is refuted. The code does what it describes, but that behaviour is the specified one, not a bug. In `PracticeService.kt:243-244`, `firstTry` counts only attempts with `missionId == mission.missionId`, so a shared task resolved in another mission is left out. The contract spec requires exactly this. In `contract/openspec/specs/practice-flow/spec.md:571-575`, the scenario "Shared task earns nothing on the summary" sets up a 10-task mission where 9 tasks were correct on the first try in this mission and task T was already resolved in another mission. It then requires the screen to show "9 na první pokus". The design doc agrees: `openspec/changes/implement-practice-flow-api/design.md:114-115` defines `firstTryCount` as "tasks resolved first try in that run through this mission". The finding's own fallback ("if the filter is intended, state that in the spec and design doc") is therefore already met. Its suggested fix, counting `CORRECT_FIRST_TRY` states across the whole scope, would break that spec scenario (it would give 10 instead of 9). The finding also cites line 1630, but the code is at line 244.

The scenario can happen, but the behaviour is documented as intended, so it is not a defect. Evidence: V3__missions.sql:3 allows a task to be in several missions (OQ-15). Model.kt:26 shares the primary scope across those missions. In PracticeService.kt:243-244, a task solved first try under mission A makes mission B COMPLETE, yet the `missionId == mission.missionId` filter leaves it out of B's firstTryCount. However, openspec/changes/implement-practice-flow-api/design.md:114-115 defines it this way on purpose: "`firstTryCount` = tasks resolved first try in that run through this mission". It also marks the summary as a slice-7 placeholder that slice 8 replaces with the gamification rules. The finding itself says that if the filter is intended it should be stated in the design doc, and it already is. So the code matches its spec, and at most the finding is a product-level question about the slice-8 rules. Also, the cited line 1630 is wrong; the code is at line 244.

The location is wrong. ServedContentService.kt has only 105 lines, and the cited code is at line 52, not line 246. The narrow mechanism is real: in `image()`, `storage.open(key)?.use { it.readAllBytes() }` does not catch IOException. Neither does `FilesystemFileStorage.open` (`Files.newInputStream`). PracticeProblemAdvice has no handler for it, so a read failure would end in a 500.

That is not a correctness defect, though:
1. User input cannot cause it. `imageId` is only used as a lookup key. The storage key comes from the database, and `locate()` enforces the storage root. Missing images and images that cannot be served are already turned into null, then 404. The rule in AGENTS.md is "No **user input** may produce a raw 500". An I/O fault on the server's own disk is a real server error, and 5xx is the right class.
2. application.yaml enables `spring.mvc.problemdetails` and sets `include-stacktrace: never`. So the response is Spring's standard error/problem body, with no driver internals or stack trace leaked. The suggested fix of returning 404 would hide a storage fault behind a misleading "not found".
3. Admin image and source serving (`TaskService` line 221, `SourceService.file`) handle storage I/O the same way. This is consistent design, not a slip specific to slice 7.

The point about reading the image into memory inside a read-only transaction is about performance or design, not correctness. Task images are small uploads with an enforced size limit. Net: the location is wrong, no user input reaches the path, and a 500 on a disk fault is acceptable behavior, so the claimed correctness bug does not hold.

The cited line is wrong: ServedContentService.kt is 105 lines long, and the code in question is at line 52. The code itself matches the finding (`storage.open(image.storageKey)?.use { it.readAllBytes() } ?: return null`, and only a handful of custom exception types are handled). Still, the claimed problem cannot be triggered by a real user or attacker:

The storage adapter (`FilesystemFileStorage.open`, line 39) does `locate(key).takeIf(Files::isRegularFile)?.let(Files::newInputStream)`, so a missing file returns null and the endpoint answers 404.
